title: strlen and memcmp
description:
Write the C library's two scanning functions with string instructions:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `scan_len(s)` | the length of the zero-terminated string `s` (with `repne scasb`) |
| `compare(a, b, n)` | 0 if the first `n` bytes are equal, otherwise the first different byte of `a` minus that of `b`, as a signed 64-bit number (with `repe cmpsb`) |

starter.solution.asm:
scan_len:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

compare:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
scan_len:
        mov     rdx, rdi
        xor     eax, eax
        mov     rcx, -1
        cld
        repne scasb
        sub     rdi, rdx
        lea     rax, [rdi - 1]
        ret

compare:
        xor     eax, eax
        mov     rcx, rdx
        test    rcx, rcx
        jz      .done
        xchg    rsi, rdi                ; cmpsb compares [rsi] with [rdi]: a must be in rsi
        cld
        repe cmpsb
        je      .done
        movzx   eax, byte [rsi - 1]
        movzx   ecx, byte [rdi - 1]
        sub     rax, rcx
.done:  ret

hints: For `scan_len`, search for the zero byte with `al` = 0 and `rcx` = −1; afterwards `rdi` points one past the zero (lesson 8.01).

`cmpsb` compares `[rsi]` with `[rdi]`, so swap the two pointers first. After `repe cmpsb` stops on a difference, the different bytes are one before where the pointers now point; use 64-bit `sub` so a negative result stays negative.
unitTests:
test "lengths"
    scan_len("hello, world") == 12
    scan_len("") == 0
    scan_len("a") == 1
test "equal"
    compare("apple", "apple", 5) == 0
    compare("apple pie", "apple tart", 6) == 0
    compare("abc", "xyz", 0) == 0
test "different"
    compare("apple pie", "apple tart", 9) == -4
    compare("b", "a", 1) == 1
    compare(b[200], b[100], 1) == 100
    compare(b[1, 2, 3], b[1, 2, 9], 3) == -6
